title: Retail loan book: early delinquency review

findings.headline: 30-day arrears rate has almost doubled in five quarters
findings.detail: The share of loans 30+ days past due at 6 months rose from 7.2% (Q1 25) to 12.8% (Q1 26), after a dip to 6.6% in Q2 25. Volumes were steady at about 1,000 loans a quarter, so this is not a mix-of-volume effect.

findings.headline: Personal and Card loans drive the deterioration
findings.detail: Personal rose from 9.3% to 21.0% and Card from 11.2% to 20.2% between Q1 25 and Q1 26. Car stayed near 6% and Home near 0.5%.

findings.headline: Shared phone numbers go with very high default and missed first payments
findings.detail: 9 phone values repeat across 42 loans. 83.3% of those loans reached 30+ days past due (about 35 loans) against 8.8% overall, and 81% missed the first payment against 2.3% overall. This is a possible fraud or duplicate-borrower signal.

findings.headline: Digital and self-employed borrowers show higher arrears
findings.detail: Digital is at 13.0% against 5.8% for Branch, and its average bureau score is lower (715.4 against 733.7). Self-employed borrowers are at 12.2% against 6.5% for salaried.

findings.headline: Income is missing for 39.7% of Partner loans
findings.detail: Income is missing in 6.9% of all rows, and 90.8% of the gaps are in the Partner channel. Any income-based analysis or affordability checks on Partner loans may be unreliable.

next_steps: Investigate the 42 loans sharing phone numbers: check applications, origination channel and branch, and consider a hold on similar new applications.
Review Personal and Card underwriting and recent cohorts, including the Digital channel mix, to see what changed from Q3 25. Also check whether the Q1 26 loans have a full 6-month window.
Ask Partner originators why income is missing, and test whether Digital and self-employed arrears hold when product is held constant.

reviews.note: 7.2% to 12.8% is about 1.8 times, not nearly double. Removed the unsupported 'not a mix effect' claim; volumes of 984 to 1,038 are steady.
Personal 9.3% to 21.0% and Card 11.2% to 20.2% confirmed. Replaced 'drive' with 'goes with'; Car 4.7-6.3% and Home 0-1.1% fit.
42 rows, 83.3% (about 35 loans) and 81% confirmed. Cut the fraud speculation and lowered severity to medium, as 35 is 8% of the 440 positives.
Digital 13.0% vs Branch 5.8%, bureau 715.4 vs 733.7, self-employed 12.2% vs salaried 6.5% all match. Medium severity is fair.
6.9% missing, 90.8% of gaps in Partner and 39.7% missing within Partner all match the summary. Medium severity is fair.

findings.headline: 30-day arrears rate rose from 7.2% to 12.8%
findings.detail: The share of loans 30 or more days past due at 6 months rose from 7.2% in Q1 25 to 12.8% in Q1 26, about 1.8 times as high. It dipped to 6.6% in Q2 25, and quarterly volumes stayed between 984 and 1,038 loans.

findings.headline: The rise goes with Personal and Card loans
findings.detail: Personal went from 9.3% to 21.0% and Card from 11.2% to 20.2% between Q1 25 and Q1 26. Car stayed between 4.7% and 6.3%, and Home stayed at or below 1.1%.

findings.headline: Shared phone numbers go with very high arrears and missed first payments
findings.detail: 9 phone values repeat across 42 loans. 83.3% of these loans (about 35) reached 30+ days past due against 8.8% overall, and 81% missed the first payment against 2.3% overall. The group is small but clearly worth checking.

findings.headline: Digital and self-employed borrowers show higher arrears
findings.detail: Digital is at 13.0% against 5.8% for Branch, and its average bureau score is lower (715.4 against 733.7). Self-employed borrowers are at 12.2% against 6.5% for salaried. Product mix has not been separated out.

findings.headline: Income is missing for 39.7% of Partner loans
findings.detail: Income is missing in 6.9% of all rows, and 90.8% of those gaps are in the Partner channel. Income-based analysis for Partner loans is less reliable.

next_steps: Review the 42 loans that share phone numbers: check their applications and how they were originated, and consider extra checks on new applications with repeated phone numbers.
Look at Personal and Card lending from Q3 25 onwards, and confirm that Q1 26 loans have had a full 6 months to show the outcome.
Test whether the Digital and self-employed gaps remain when product is held constant, and ask Partner originators why income is missing.
conclusion: Early arrears have risen from 7.2% to 12.8% over five quarters, and the rise goes with Personal and Card loans rather than Car or Home. First, check whether the Q1 26 figure is complete and comparable, then review Personal and Card lending since Q3 25. The shared-phone group is small but has very high arrears and deserves a separate look.
limits: This review uses summary statistics only, so it cannot show why arrears rose, whether channel or employment gaps survive once product is allowed for, or whether recent quarters have fully matured.
